ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl:
Let n>1 be an integer and let t be a real number with 0<=t<1.

By the defining property of the floor function, floor(n t)=n-1 if and only if
n-1 <= n t < n.
So it remains to translate these inequalities into a condition on t.

First, if floor(n t)=n-1, then n-1 <= n t. Since n>0, dividing by n gives
(n-1)/n <= t.
Because t already satisfies t<1 by hypothesis, we obtain (n-1)/n <= t <1.

Conversely, if (n-1)/n <= t <1, then multiplying by the positive integer n yields
n-1 <= n t < n.
Applying the floor characterization again, this implies floor(n t)=n-1.

Thus, for every integer n>1 and every real t with 0<=t<1,
floor(n t)=n-1 if and only if (n-1)/n <= t <1.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n with n > 1 and all real numbers t with 0 <= t < 1: floor(n*t) equals n-1 exactly when t is at least (n-1)/n and still less than 1.
witness_dependencies: no existential witnesses are introduced; the statement is a pure equivalence between a condition on floor(n*t) and a condition on t
